newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity steady to lower.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West were trading steady to lower with mild temperatures dominating the region, industry sources said.
Little next-day business was said to be done in the Mid-West with sellers reluctant to part with electricity at the low prices, the brokers and marketers said.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), on peak electricity for a 16-hour block for delivery Thursday was talked in the $15.00-17.00 range, with off-peak power in the region pegged near $8.50, the sources said.

On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Thursday delivery were also said to be discussed at $15.00-17.00, with off-peak power pegged near $11.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Thursday delivery were quoted steady in the $14.00-16.00 range, the sources said.
Cheap next-day ECAR peak power was said to be dragging longer term prices lower, with the remainder of September discussed near $15.50 and October at close to $17.00.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Thursday delivery was assessed in the $16.00-16.50 range in the southern area of the region, with off-peak power pegged in the $14.00-15.00 range.
In the northern area of SPP, power was talked in the $13.00-14.00 range, with off-peak electricity discussed in the 10.50-12.50 range, the brokers and marketers said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
